_meta.indication: PERJETA is indicated for use in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel for the treatment of patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who have not received prior anti-HER2 therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 1:1 to receive placebo plus trastuzumab and docetaxel or PERJETA plus trastuzumab and docetaxel.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who had not received HER2-directed therapy or chemotherapy in the metastatic setting; HER2 overexpression required (3+ IHC or FISH ratio >= 2.0).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by an independent review facility (IRF).
pivotal_trials.n: 808 patients (PERJETA arm n=402; placebo arm n=406)
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant improvement in IRF-assessed PFS: HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.51, 0.75), p < 0.0001; median PFS 18.5 months (PERJETA) vs 12.4 months (placebo), a 6.1-month improvement. Interim OS HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.47, 0.88), p=0.0053 (did not meet stopping boundary). ORR 80.2% vs 69.3%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>30%) were diarrhea, alopecia, neutropenia, nausea, fatigue, rash, and peripheral neuropathy. Most common Grade 3-4 reactions (>2%) included neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, leukopenia, diarrhea, peripheral neuropathy, anemia, asthenia, and fatigue. Diarrhea 66.8% (vs 46.3%), neutropenia 52.8% (vs 49.6%), febrile neutropenia 13.8% (vs 7.6%).
target_moa: Pertuzumab targets the extracellular dimerization domain (Subdomain II) of HER2, blocking ligand-dependent heterodimerization of HER2 with other HER family members (EGFR, HER3, HER4), thereby inhibiting intracellular signaling through the MAP kinase and PI3K pathways; it also mediates ADCC.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — Exposure to PERJETA can result in embryo-fetal death and birth defects. Studies in animals have resulted in oligohydramnios, delayed renal development, and death. Advise patients of these risks and the need for effective contraception.

rems.type: No REMS or Medication Guide is required for marketing of pertuzumab.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Agency did not believe outside expertise was necessary and there were no controversial clinical issues.

description.text: Updated labeling to include second interim overall survival analysis for pertuzumab in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for updating the package insert to include the results of the second interim analysis of overall survival for the indication for use in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel for the treatment of patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer who have not received prior anti-HER2 therapy or chemotherapy for metastatic disease.

description.text: Granted accelerated approval for use in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel for the neoadjuvant treatment of HER2-positive, locally advanced, inflammatory, or early stage breast cancer

citations.quote:
Proposed Indication(s)	PERJETA is indicated for use in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel for the neoadjuvant treatment of patients with HER2-positive, locally advanced, inflammatory, or early stage breast cancer (either greater than 2 cm in diameter or node positive) as part of a complete treatment regimen for early breast cancer. This indication is based on demonstration of an improvement in pathological complete response rate. No data are available demonstrating improvement in event-free survival or overall survival.
Action/Recommended Action for NME:	Accelerated Approval

summary.text: Perjeta (pertuzumab) received a traditional (full) approval under Priority review as a new molecular entity BLA, supported primarily by the single phase 3 CLEOPATRA trial demonstrating a statistically significant PFS improvement; no advisory committee was convened, and no accelerated approval or other special designation was applied.

The pertuzumab BLA is primarily supported by a single, multinational, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized phase 3 study (CLEOPATRA; TOC4129g; WO20698).

Your application for pertuzumab was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the Agency did not believe that outside expertise was necessary; there were no controversial clinical issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.
